subject.title: feat(process): add starvation guard to priority command queue

question: Should aged lower-priority command-queue work ever overtake fresh foreground/user work after the starvation threshold?
rationale: The central behavior is a product scheduler policy: the linked issue asks for no indefinite low-priority starvation, while current implementation preserves foreground dominance and therefore does not satisfy the steady-foreground starvation claim.

options.title: Choose True Bounded Starvation
options.body: Aged background or normal work can overtake fresh foreground after the threshold, and the PR should update code, tests, comments, and proof to that contract.

options.title: Choose Foreground-Preserving Aging
options.body: Keep one-tier aging so user work always wins, but narrow the PR wording and leave the stronger starvation request open.

options.title: Pause For Broader Scheduler Work
options.body: Defer this PR behind the broader queue fairness items if maintainers want foreground reserve, origin-aware scheduling, and aging handled together.

recommendation.title: Choose True Bounded Starvation
recommendation.body: Aged background or normal work can overtake fresh foreground after the threshold, and the PR should update code, tests, comments, and proof to that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and hardened the original queue path and recently closed the overlapping scheduler PR while pointing the remaining aging policy to this focused PR.
